findings.reason: Verified: pipeline.signature is an md5 of the view class names, so it is the same for every user, and line 412 accepts any request carrying that value. A forged callback with an attacker's code passes the check and binds the attacker's login, which can defeat the installer check at line 502.

Verified: build_integration sets metadata["sender"] only when state has a sender, and only the webhook supplies one, so a pipeline-created Integration lacks it; line 503 then raises KeyError on a later reinstall where the Integration exists without an OrganizationIntegration. The path is narrower than stated but real.

Verified: safe_urlopen (line 423) sits outside the try, and get_user_info (line 434) is unwrapped and calls raise_for_status(), so a network or HTTP error propagates as an uncaught 500 instead of rendering the error template.

The gap is real but pre-existing: the Integration-not-found branch went straight to next_step() before this PR and the PR does not make it worse, so this is a pre-existing issue rather than a defect the PR introduces.

Verified in the test: lines 388-396 send state ddd023... (not the signature 9cae5e...), so the request fails at the state check and the 404 installation path is no longer exercised, although the test is still named test_installation_not_found.
